data.long_meaning: Valian is a Latin name meaning 'strong' or 'healthy'. It is derived from the Latin word "valius", which means 'of good health' or 'strong'. In the Christian tradition, the name Valian is often associated with the virtue of courage and strength. The name Valian carries the meaning “Valiant, Strong, Healthy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Valian usually hope their child will grow to embody valiant, strong, healthy and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is not uncommon for individuals with this name to be seen as leaders and protectors, inherrent with a Character of fearlessness in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: Biblically, Valian may be associated with the Old Testament warrior David, who displayed great courage and strength in his battles and ultimately became a king of Israel. As Christians, we are called to be worthy heirs and imitators of Jesus Christ, who himself displayed immeasurable strength and courage on the cross for our salvation. Therefore, the name Valian may serve as a reminder to live out our faith with unwavering strength and courage.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Valian: Derived from the Latin word "valere," meaning "to be strong" or "to be healthy," Valian is a Christian name that symbolizes strength, courage, and endurance in the face of challenges. historical_references.reference: Saint Valian of Saragossa, also known as Valerianus or Valeriano, was a bishop and martyr during the Roman persecutions of the early 3rd century. He is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church.

Saint Valian of Brives-et-Peschieres was a hermit and later abbot in the late 5th or early 6th century. He is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church and his relics are kept in the monastery of Brives-et-Peschieres in France.
